comment: Per-resort corrections applied by pipeline/normalize_osm.py (ADR-036). See whistler-blackcomb.overrides.json for the format. One polygon, relation/18484946 (Sugarloaf, three outer ways): the lift-served mountain from the Snowfields above the lifts to the base village, West Mountain and the Snubber lift on one ticket and one map. Maine Huts and Trails (way/1233552674), a separate non-profit's hut-to-hut network whose polygon reaches into the box's north edge, is a listed neighbour in resorts.json and holds nothing of the resort's; the Sugarloaf Outdoor Center (way/1233552673, the resort's own nordic centre) is the resort's and not a neighbour, and its nordic trails are left out by the type rule. Every named run and lift checked on 2026-11-12 against Sugarloaf's 2025-26 winter trail map (sugarloaf.com/mountain-info, 'Trail Map', the James Niehues painting, the PDF made 2025-11-12): one 1530 x 1323 pt page, the painting with its Snowfields inset (front side with the six chutes and the back side's numbered lines 70 to 74) and its Burnt Mountain, Eastern Territory and Brackett Basin panels; its labels are drawn as outlines over a 72 dpi copy of the painting, so it was rendered at 300 dpi and read tile by tile, the doubtful places at 400 to 600 dpi. Its key: Experts Only (two black diamonds, 'use extreme caution'), Most Difficult (one), More Difficult (blue square), Easier (green circle), Wild Things (not groomed), Slow and Family Skiing, Friendliest Way Down, Freestyle Terrain (orange pills), and line styles for the Ski Area Boundary (red dashes), Golden Road, the Burnt Mountain Trail, Whiffletree Egress, King Pine X-Cut, Snubber Egress, the logging and cat roads; 80 glades and connecting trails are numbered, named in the key and drawn in their grade's colour without symbols. The resort's mountain report loads its trail status by script, so the printed map is the only source and wins. OSM's easy, intermediate, advanced and expert are the map's four grades. Ratings: Haywire (advanced) and the east way of Tote Road Crosscut (easy) to intermediate, the middle way of Upper Scoot (easy) to intermediate, the east way of Bucksaw X-Cut (intermediate) to easy, and Rough Cut Glade (advanced) to expert with the rest of Brackett Basin. Brackett Basin, the Eastern Territory and Burnt Mountain lie inside the map's boundary (the brief's rule: in bounds only where the map draws them inside it), so their three run areas (rated expert, the zones' two diamonds, and named Brackett Basin and Burnt Mountain as the map labels them) and their 15 lines OSM tags backcountry (Golden Road, the glades, Logging Road and the Whiffletree and Snubber egresses) are kept in bounds by overrides, with OSM's ratings on the lines; the Snowfields' chutes lie inside OSM's polygon or carry no backcountry tag and are in bounds already, and the back side's lines 70 to 74, which the map numbers without symbols, keep OSM's ratings (Awesome extreme, the others expert). Names from the map: Hard Tack (OSM Hard Track), Hayburner (Hayburnder), Natalie's Birches (Birches Slope), Beaver Tail (the upper way's Beaver Trail), Androscoggin Glade (Adroscoggin), Cant Dog 1 and 2 (Can't Dog), Whiffletree Egress (Wiffletree), Brackett Basin and Burnt Mountain for the areas, the Double Runner West lift (Doubble) and Snubber for the lift's lower way (Snubber Lower); the '[condo access]' note is hidden as a name. Names that differ from the map only by an abbreviation, a word or a section stay as OSM has them: the U., M. and L. names, Upper and Lower Poleline (U. and L. POLE LINE), Tote Road Crosscut (TOTE ROAD X-CUT), Edger 1 and 2 and Sweeper 1 (EDGER and SWEEPER GLADE), Sheer Boom (the map's 31 Upper Sheer Boom and SHEER BOOM along the SuperQuad, both black), Whiffletree SuperQuad (WHIFFLETREE). Kept as OSM has them after checking the lines: Candy Side's lower way (easy: the map's blue Candy Side ends at the green run to the base), Upper Whiffletree's top way (intermediate: the short blue line between Jill Poke and Rollway at the lift's top), and runs the map draws unlabelled or not at all (Stomping Ground, Pipeline, Winter's Way Crosscut, the west way of Tote Road Crosscut). Parks: none flagged. The map's orange pills (S/M, M, S, L, BX) sit on rated trails drawn in their own colours, and a park flag would draw the whole trail as a park, as at Killington; its one named park, The Yard (M/L), is not in OSM. Lifts: the map's A to N are in OSM (Whiffletree, Sugarloaf SuperQuad, Bucksaw Express, King Pine, Timberline, Skyline, Snubber in two ways, Skidway, Sawduster, Double Runner East and West, West Mountain, Bateau T-Bar, Moosecalator). OSM gaps (shipped as at Palisades Tahoe): the CVA Colby T-Bar (lift O); The Yard; L. Sheer Boom, L. Skidder and L. Double Bitter; Skid Road; Rookie River and Lower Rookie River; Drop Line (closed to skiing); the glades Cant Hook, Blade, Stump Shot, Fred's Pitch, Boomer, Kickback, Swedish Fiddle, Raker Tooth, Broccoli Garden, Stub's, Blueberry's Grove, Kerf, Ram Pasture, Boomscooter, Barber Chair, Jackpot, Branding Ax, Greenhorn, Gondi, Alice's Winterland, Red Horse, Blacksmith, High Ball and Slashfire; the King Pine X-Cut and the Burnt Mountain Trail.

overrides.reason: Haywire, from Peavy X-Cut down to the lower Candy Side above the base, is a blue line with a blue square (More Difficult) on Sugarloaf's 2025-26 winter trail map (sugarloaf.com/mountain-info, 'Trail Map', the James Niehues painting, the PDF made 2025-11-12); OSM rates it advanced. The printed map wins.

The east way of Bucksaw X-Cut (104 m, to the Lower Timberline corridor): Sugarloaf's 2025-26 winter trail map (sugarloaf.com/mountain-info, 'Trail Map', the James Niehues painting, the PDF made 2025-11-12) draws Bucksaw X-Cut (trail 36) as one green line with a green circle (Easier); OSM rates its west way easy and this one intermediate. The printed map wins.

The middle way of Upper Scoot (74 m, where Good Chance X-Cut leaves it): Sugarloaf's 2025-26 winter trail map (sugarloaf.com/mountain-info, 'Trail Map', the James Niehues painting, the PDF made 2025-11-12) draws U. SCOOT as one blue line with a blue square (More Difficult) from Spurline down to Horseshoe; OSM rates its two other ways intermediate and this one easy. The printed map wins.

The east way of Tote Road Crosscut (177 m, across the SuperQuad line from the Double Runner West top): Sugarloaf's 2025-26 winter trail map (sugarloaf.com/mountain-info, 'Trail Map', the James Niehues painting, the PDF made 2025-11-12) draws trail 47, TOTE ROAD X-CUT, there as a blue line with a blue square (More Difficult) between Lower Spillway and Upper Competition Hill; OSM rates it easy. The printed map wins. (Its 575 m west way, which the map does not draw, keeps OSM's easy.)

The map's grade, the harder, wins.

OSM's polygon covers the lift-served front only and tags this terrain backcountry, so it would draw out of bounds. In bounds, as the map draws it; named BRACKETT BASIN and rated Experts Only (two diamonds) from the map (OSM advanced).
